title: Talent Ops Coordinator - 30 Day Launch Plan
summary: A compact hiring and onboarding playbook for the Talent Operations Coordinator role: designed for a fast, measurable ramp with a strong mentor loop and operational checklists. Focus areas: interview rubric, 48-hour trial assignment, a prioritized day-by-day 30-day activation timeline, and success metrics for handoff to TA operations.
purpose: Create a repeatable interview + 30-day onboarding flow that reduces time-to-productivity and standardizes evidence for conversion decisions. This doc is an opinionated working playbook to be used by People Ops hiring owners and hiring managers during Q4 hiring sprints.
hire_profile: Early-career to mid-level operations generalist with 1-3 years experience in recruiting ops, HRIS tasks, scheduling orchestration, or program coordination. Comfortable with ambiguity, strong attention to detail, pragmatic communicator, basic scripting or Google Sheets automation preferred.
hiring_plan: 1) Sourcing + prescreen (3 days): Recruiter screens for logistics experience and scheduling volume. 2) Ops-sense phone screen (30 mins): hiring owner focuses on past workflows, toolset familiarity (Greenhouse, GCal, Slack), and availability. 3) Assignment (48 hours): short trial focused on calendar orchestration + spreadsheet cleansing. 4) Structured on-site (2 hours remote): behavioral + practical simulation with Hiring Manager and People Ops partner. 5) Decision and offer (2 days). Total elapsed target: 10 business days.
interview_rubric: Scoring: 1-5 scale across four dimensions. Anchors included. Dimension 1 - Operational Rigor (1=no process examples, 5=owned multi-step ops with measurable outcomes). Dimension 2 - Communication & Stakeholder Mgmt (1=unclear, 5=proactive, sets expectations, escalates appropriately). Dimension 3 - Tooling & Automation Aptitude (1=no tool exposure, 5=advanced Sheets/short scripts/workflow automation). Dimension 4 - Cultural Fit & Growth Mindset (1=reluctant to feedback, 5=seeks feedback and documents learnings). Pass threshold: average >=4 and no dimension <=2. Hiring manager to write 2-line justification aligned to rubric evidence.
sample_questions: Tell me about a time you prevented a scheduling meltdown — what steps did you take and what was the outcome?
Walk through how you'd clean up a recruiter calendar with duplicated events and unclear titles for a hiring wave of 20 roles.
Describe a small automation/shortcut you built to save your team time. How did you measure impact?
How do you prioritize when multiple stakeholders ask for conflicting scheduling constraints? Give a concrete example.
assignment_trial: Deliverables (48h): 1) Given a mock CSV of 150 candidates with inconsistent status/title columns, return a cleaned, normalized sheet and a 6-line runbook describing assumptions and edge-cases. 2) Provide a 10-step calendar orchestration plan for a 3-day onsite for 6 candidates across 3 interviewers with conflicting blocks. Scoring: completeness (30%), clarity of runbook (30%), edge-case handling (20%), speed of delivery (20%).
onboarding_checklist: Pre-start: access provisioning request to IT and People Tools (Greenhouse, Lattice, GSuite, Slack) submitted 5 days prior.
Day 0: Welcome email, team intro channel, equipment checklist delivered, calendar of first week added.
Day 1-3: Shadow scheduling & offer workflow with People Ops buddy; complete HRIS refresher and security training.
Week 1: Ownership of 1 small recruiter wave scheduling end-to-end with mentor oversight; join biweekly People Ops standup.
Week 2: Handover of candidate CSV cleanup project from assignment into recurring script / macro; start running weekly metrics snapshot.
Weeks 3-4: Lead coordination for one cross-functional hire (from req creation to offer); draft a one-page playbook for the hiring manager.
End of 30 days: 30-day review with hiring manager and People Ops lead; agree on PDP and autonomy gate for independent coordination.
Ongoing: weekly 1:1 for first 8 weeks; document process improvements in shared People Ops Playbook.
first_30_day_timeline: Days 0-3: Access + observation; complete trial shadow checklist
Days 4-7: Take ownership of micro-task (scheduler wave of 5 roles)
Week 2: Introduce first process improvement (sheet template or event naming scheme)
Weeks 3-4: Lead an end-to-end coordination with minimal intervention; prepare 30-day report
mentor_pledge: Assigned mentor will: review all candidate communications for first 10 days, provide daily 15-min check-ins for week 1, and complete a rubric-based readout at day 10 and day 30. Mentor must document 3 coaching points and 2 concrete next steps after each readout.
success_metrics: Scheduling error rate: < 2% (no double-books that impact interviews)
Assignment-to-hire conversion signal: trial assignment pass rate > 80% for hires made
Process improvement adoption: at least one documented improvement merged to People Ops Playbook within 30 days
notes: Open decisions: whether to require the assignment for internal candidates; compensation band alignment to be confirmed with Finance; consider adding a 15-minute asynchronous Slack scenario as an alternative to the live phone screen for scheduling flexibility.
